services.name: Online Exhibit
services.desc: To assist in the final push to finish the Shrine of the North American Martyrs, two large fundraisers were held; one in 1937, and this one in 1938. This is a full copy of the program for the 1938 fundraiser, held at the Putnam Valley Central School (now the elementary school). It’s a wonderful peek into Putnam Valley 80 years ago, giving a good idea of life at the time and the businesses our residents would frequent. There’s even a listing for Sears Roebuck & Co! We are fortunate enough to have photos of several of the businesses listed - some buildings are still around today! O’Connor’s Restaurant would later be destroyed a little over a month after the fundraiser was held. The fundraiser

blurb: We are the Putnam Valley Historical Society, founded in 1968, when the approaching bicentennial of the American Revolution was heightening everyone’s awareness of history. In 1975, the residents of the Central School District voted to give the old one-room schoolhouse at Adams Corners to the Town.
